activity.notes: Croesus was the last independent king of Lydia, ruling from Sardis until the Persian conquest by Cyrus the Great. Modern museum chronology commonly places his reign at approximately 560-546 BCE. ATLAS therefore records both boundaries as approximate rather than converting the conventional chronology into exact accession and deposition years.

sources.title: Sardis — The Metropolitan Museum of Art
sources.citation_text: The Metropolitan Museum identifies Croesus as the last Lydian king and states that he ruled Lydia from around 560 to 546 BCE, before the Persian conquest of Sardis.

sources.title: Lydia and Phrygia — The Metropolitan Museum of Art
sources.citation_text: The Metropolitan Museum describes Lydia as an independent kingdom centered on Sardis and records its conquest by Cyrus in 546 BCE during the time of King Croesus.
